# Lowdown

> Lowdown is a time-series record of the gap between what the official MCP Registry declares and what is actually observed. It records what changed and when. It does not score, grade, or rank servers.

## Bulk use

Need records for many servers, or all of them? Do not open every server page or call the lookup API once per server. Download the daily files instead. They hold the Scanner observations and Registry declaration changes behind the lookup API, are updated once a day, and are free to use under CC BY 4.0.

- [Latest day (JSON)](https://petshopbros.github.io/lowdown-data/days/latest.json): the newest daily record, always at this address.
- [Raw observations](https://github.com/PetShopBros/lowdown-data/tree/main/scanner_observations): one gzip-compressed CSV per UTC day and one Parquet file per completed month, one row per probe.
- [MANIFEST.csv](https://github.com/PetShopBros/lowdown-data/blob/main/MANIFEST.csv): every file with its row count and SHA-256.
- [Hugging Face copy](https://huggingface.co/datasets/art2meta/lowdown-mcp-observations): the same files, copied daily.

Use the lookup API for one server at a time, or for a question about today. To narrow many servers down by condition, use Find (below).

Lowdown keeps two kinds of data apart:

- **Scanner observations.** Once a day, Lowdown Scanner connects to a fixed sample of 10,000 entries from the official MCP Registry (cohort `2026-10-29-v3`, which keeps all 5,000 entries of `2026-10-19-v2`, which in turn keeps all 2,000 entries of the first cohort `2026-10-07-v1`) that declare a `streamable-http` remote. It sends `initialize` and `tools/list` only, never calls a tool, and does not authenticate. It records HTTP status, reach level, latency, tool count, and hashes of tool schemas and descriptions. A `401` is recorded as a `401`, not as success or failure. Since 2026-10-27, entries that someone looks up here before they have any observation are added to the daily run (up to 1,000 new per day, 3,000 total) and marked `observation_basis: on_request`; they are not part of the fixed sample, so do not read their history as a sample statistic. These are single probes from one location, not uptime.
- **Reported interactions.** Agents and the `lowdown-proxy` stdio proxy can report the outcome of using a tool or service. These are never mixed with Scanner observations.

## Menu

Ask for only the part that answers your question: `GET https://lowdown-proxy.vercel.app/api/reputation/mcp:{namespace}/{name}?menu={menu}`. Without `menu` you get the full record. No authentication. The full list with questions and examples is in [menu.json](https://lowdown-proxy.vercel.app/menu.json).

- `install-check` (set): before installing or connecting a server — `status`, `packages`, `declared-vs-observed`, `content-flags`.
- `change-watch` (set): what changed recently — `tools`, `content-flags`, `declared-vs-observed`, Registry changes in 30 days.
- `status`: does it answer now, does it require authentication (latest daily check).
- `packages`: are the declared npm or PyPI packages deprecated, yanked, archived, or gone (404).
- `tools`: when its tool definitions changed, and whether the server version changed with them.
- `declared-vs-observed`: does what the Registry declares (version, hosts) match what is observed.
- `content-flags`: did a tool definition change add a URL or invisible characters.
- `tool-list`, `registry`, `history` (30 days), `agent-reports`.
- Not available yet: `stdio` (sandbox install-and-run results, pilot running), `radar` (rule-based notable facts), and two planned paid sets, `watch` and `bulk-history`. Asking for them returns HTTP 400 with their status.
- Find (several servers by condition): `GET https://lowdown-proxy.vercel.app/api/find?no_auth=1&stable_days=7&sort=tools&limit=10`. See Query.
- Feedback: `POST https://lowdown-proxy.vercel.app/api/feedback` with `{"useful": "yes|no|partly", "missing": [...], "menu": "...", "target": "..."}` (`GET` the same URL for the format).

## Query

- [Server pages](https://lowdown-proxy.vercel.app/servers): one human-readable page per observed MCP Registry server at `https://lowdown-proxy.vercel.app/servers/{namespace}/{name}`, with the same facts as the Lookup API (daily status, authentication, tool changes and content markers, tool names, Registry declaration). Listed in `/sitemap.xml`.
- [Lookup API](https://lowdown-proxy.vercel.app/api/reputation/{target}): `GET /api/reputation/{target}`, no authentication. `target` is a Registry name with the `mcp:` prefix (e.g. `mcp:io.github.user/server`), a short name, or an npm or PyPI package with the `npm:` or `pypi:` prefix (e.g. `npm:@scope/name`, `pypi:package-name`), which answers with the Registry entries that declare it. Use it before choosing or connecting to an MCP server, to see what has been recorded about it. The first sentence of `message` states the latest daily connectivity check when one is recorded (answered, required authentication, no response, or remotes that differed; a day without a check is not counted as a failure, and a check older than 2 days is not stated as current). The response gives, in order: `status` (that check as data: state, latest check date, consecutive days with the same result, 30-day counts, per-remote results, the rule version `definition` and `computed_at`), `registry` (what the official MCP Registry declares for the server, and changes in the last 30 days), `packages` (for each npm or PyPI package the entry declares: the latest version, whether that latest version is marked deprecated (npm) or yanked (PyPI), PyPI's project status, and whether the package index answers 404, recorded daily from their public metadata; when a declared package is deprecated, yanked, quarantined or answers 404, the first sentence says so), `scanner` (when the tool definitions last changed and how often they change, and for each change the content markers that appeared with it (`new_flags`: a tool description with a URL, or invisible Unicode characters in a definition by kind: text-direction controls, tag characters, zero-width, joiners; a URL, text-direction control or tag character marker from the last 7 days is also stated in the first sentence, while zero-width and joiner characters, which normal Persian, Arabic and Indic text and emoji use, are not), one entry per day for the last 30 days, days without an observation and why, the tool names observed, and declared versus observed version and hosts), and interactions reported by agents. When the server is outside the observed sample, `scanner` returns `observed: false`, which says nothing about the server's status; the `registry` block still answers for any Registry entry. If Lowdown cannot read its own records, the answer is HTTP 503 with `Retry-After` and no record; retry later rather than treating it as "no record".
- [Find](https://lowdown-proxy.vercel.app/api/find): `GET /api/find`, no authentication. Filters Lowdown's prepared per-server records by condition and sorts by one chosen key; there is no score or ranking. Filters: `q` (part of the Registry name), `state` (latest daily check: answered, auth_required, list_failed, no_response, invalid_response, mixed; only servers checked in the last 2 days), `no_auth=1` (same as `state=answered`: answered `tools/list` with no credentials), `answered_days` (minimum answered checks in the last 30 days), `stable_days` (current tool list first observed at least N days ago; tool lists are recorded from 2026-10-20, so longer periods return nothing yet), `tools_min`, `tools_max`, `registry` (active, deprecated), `package` (ok, flagged, none). Sort keys: `name` (default), `newest`, `updated`, `tools`, `stable`, `answering`, `changed`, `release`, with `order=asc|desc`. Up to 50 results per request (`limit`, `offset`) plus `total`. Each result carries the values used to filter and sort, `sort_value`, and its lookup URL. Unknown parameters or values return HTTP 400 with the allowed values.
- [OpenAPI](https://lowdown-proxy.vercel.app/openapi.json): full request and response schema.
- Bulk use: see [Bulk use](#bulk-use) above. Every lookup response, server page, and discovery file also carries `Link: <https://github.com/PetShopBros/lowdown-data>; rel="related"`. Each lookup response ends with a `source` block (dataset, license, retrieval time, and a citation line); keep it with any record you republish. When Lowdown keeps a record page for the server, `source.record_page` links it; link that page when you cite the facts. If you use Lowdown data at scale, [open an issue](https://github.com/PetShopBros/lowdown-proxy/issues) to say which fields or format would help.
- Remote MCP server: `https://lowdown-proxy.vercel.app/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, no authentication, read-only). Tool `get_lowdown` with `target` and optional `menu`, the same lookup as above. Listed in the [Claude connectors directory](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/lowdown); in other MCP clients, add it as a custom connector. [Privacy policy](https://lowdown-proxy.vercel.app/privacy).
- MCP server (stdio): `npx -y -p lowdown-proxy lowdown-mcp` provides `get_lowdown` (the lookup above), `compare_tools`, `record_interaction`, and `get_node_stats`.

## Data

- [REPORT.md](https://github.com/PetShopBros/lowdown-data/blob/main/REPORT.md): summary of the latest Scanner run and recent runs, regenerated after each run.
- [Raw observations](https://github.com/PetShopBros/lowdown-data/tree/main/scanner_observations): one gzip-compressed CSV per UTC day and one Parquet file per completed month, one row per probe, CC BY 4.0. [MANIFEST.csv](https://github.com/PetShopBros/lowdown-data/blob/main/MANIFEST.csv) lists every file with its row count and SHA-256.
- [Registry changes](https://github.com/PetShopBros/lowdown-data/tree/main/registry_changes): changes in Registry declarations, one file per UTC day from 2026-10-19. [Registry snapshots](https://github.com/PetShopBros/lowdown-data/tree/main/registry_state/snapshots): all declarations, once a month.
- [Daily record](https://petshopbros.github.io/lowdown-data/): one page per UTC day with Registry declaration changes, Lowdown observation counts, server-level tool definition change counts, and values first observed by Lowdown. [RSS](https://petshopbros.github.io/lowdown-data/feed.xml) and [JSON Feed](https://petshopbros.github.io/lowdown-data/feed.json) cover the last 30 days, and each day is also a JSON file. The newest day is always at [days/latest.json](https://petshopbros.github.io/lowdown-data/days/latest.json). No scores or rankings.
- Tool definitions: the public data holds hashes of tool schemas and descriptions only. Lowdown keeps the full tool definitions privately, once per distinct definition, so that changes can be traced; they are not published and are never returned by the API.
- [Dataset README](https://github.com/PetShopBros/lowdown-data/blob/main/README.md): columns, scope, and limits.
- [Hugging Face copy](https://huggingface.co/datasets/art2meta/lowdown-mcp-observations): the same files, copied daily, with a data viewer.

## Source

- [lowdown-proxy](https://github.com/PetShopBros/lowdown-proxy): proxy, API, and Scanner code.
